title: Multi-Objective Genetic-Algorithm-Based Trajectory Optimization for Data Collection in Mobile Wireless Sensor Networks
content: This paper presents a method for determining an optimized data-collection trajectory in mobile wireless sensor networks. Energy conservation is a central challenge because network lifetime depends strongly on communication and routing costs. The proposed method formulates trajectory planning as a multi-objective optimization problem involving four simultaneous objectives: minimization of trajectory length and energy consumption; maximization of information gathered from critical sensors located near the monitored target; avoidance of hops that exceed the communication range; and avoidance of sensors with critically low residual energy. Because the resulting problem is combinatorial, a multi-objective genetic algorithm is employed. The method is evaluated against a conventional genetic algorithm, Local Closest First, and Global Closest First. Simulation results indicate that the proposed method provides the lowest overall cost while satisfying sensing, communication, and residual-energy constraints.
